title: It means 'picture character'.
description:
It means 'picture character'. From Japanese: e, picture, plus moji, character. That it sounds like 'emoticon' is an accident of English. The two words share no root at all.

Shigetaka Kurita's 1999 set for DoCoMo, drawn on a grid of twelve pixels by twelve. The originals are now held by the Museum of Modern Art.

A rival set beat it by two years. SoftBank, then called J-Phone, shipped 90 emoji on a 1997 handset, before DoCoMo's 176. Kurita himself has said DoCoMo was not first.

A word that is not about feelings, pinned to a set that was not first.

Sources:
- https://www.etymonline.com/word/emoji - Online Etymology Dictionary, via search summary. Established that "emoji" is from Japanese e (picture) plus moji (character), meaning "pictograph", and that the resemblance to English "emoticon" and "emotion" is coincidental, the words being unrelated in origin.
- https://www.moma.org/collection/works/196070 - The Museum of Modern Art, via search summary. Established that Shigetaka Kurita designed a set of 176 emoji in 1998 to 1999 for NTT DoCoMo's i-mode on a grid of twelve by twelve pixels, and that MoMA holds the set in its collection.
- https://blog.emojipedia.org/correcting-the-record-on-the-first-emoji-set/ - Emojipedia, via search summary. Established that SoftBank (then J-Phone) released a set of 90 emoji in 1997, two years before DoCoMo's 176, and that Kurita himself has said DoCoMo was not the first, correcting the common "first emoji" claim.
